the-big-parade-1925_202505: I've been researching newly public domain films from 1929 and earlier, so I'm uploading the best possible copies that I can find. rv: The Great War was hellish, and despite being silent, this movie delivers

"All Quiet On the Western Front" is practically a sound remake of "The Big Crowd," the narrative arc is very similar (innocent patriotic men quickly coming to the realization that war is hell), and certain scenes, like the soldiers cavorting with French women in exchange for food, seem like outright steals. Both movies are excellent, however; and well worth your attention. King Vidor, the director of "The Big Parade," made another underrated silent classic in 1928 called "The Crowd" which I highly recommend as well. The opening sequence is amazing, in particular for its time period.
